rounds.text: Promax Power Ltd presents a compelling deep-value opportunity supported by tangible asset backing, trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.93x with a price of ₹ 11.5 against a book value of ₹ 12.4 [E2]. The underlying business demonstrates structural top-line resilience, evidenced by a year-on-year sales growth of 9% and a multi-year sales uptrend [E61, E62]. This top-line expansion is underpinned by a strong historical earnings track record, featuring a compounded profit growth of 34% over 5 years and 16% over 3 years, which easily outpaces the sector median profit growth of 11.6% [E17, E18, E70]. Furthermore, the micro-cap market capitalization of ₹ 28.8 Cr leaves the company undiscovered and primed for re-rating [E3]. Conceded: the stock currently sits at the absolute bottom of its 52-week range, reflecting severe recent sentiment compression [E5], and trailing twelve-month profit growth has contracted by 63% [E19].

The current valuation of Promax Power Ltd is heavily disconnected from its fundamental deterioration, highlighted by a trailing twelve months compounded profit growth of -63% [E19]. While historical compounding looked solid at 34% over 5 years [E17], earnings growth is now decelerating [E65], causing price growth to outpace profit delivery by 2% [E52]. This slowdown leaves the company trading at an alarming P/E of 72.58x against a sector benchmark of just 15.99x [E6], alongside a price-to-book ratio of 2.4x that severely undercuts the sector benchmark of 1.33x [E7]. Operational efficiency also lags behind the broader market, evidenced by a return on assets of 2.3% compared to the sector benchmark of 2.82% [E8]. Furthermore, the stock offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4] and sits entirely at the bottom of its 52-week range at 0% of its span from a 12 low to a 34 high [E5], signalling profound lack of support from the market. Conceded: the company displays a price-to-book ratio of 0.93x at a price of ₹ 11.5 on a book value of ₹ 12.4 [E2], alongside a 5-year compounded profit growth of 34% [E17] and a 3-year compounded profit growth of 16% [E18].
